question: Who founded the Maurya Empire by overthrowing the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, with the guidance of his mentor Chanakya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta Maurya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 322 BCE by overthrowing Dhana Nanda, the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, with the strategic guidance of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya/Vishnugupta). (मौर्य साम्राज्य के संस्थापक — चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य)

 

• He established his capital at Pataliputra and later expanded the empire after defeating the Greek satrap Seleucus Nikator, gaining territories up to the Hindu Kush.

 

• Towards the end of his reign, Chandragupta is traditionally said to have embraced Jainism, abdicated the throne to his son Bindusara, and died at Shravanabelagola as an ascetic under Bhadrabahu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chanakya, also known as Kautilya, was Chandragupta's mentor and prime minister, and is traditionally credited as the author of the Arthashastra, a treatise on statecraft, economics and military strategy.

 

NOTE

 

• Bindusara (Option 1): The second Mauryan ruler, son of Chandragupta Maurya; extended the empire further into the Deccan.

 

• Ashoka (Option 2): The third Mauryan ruler, grandson of Chandragupta, famed for the Kalinga War (261 BCE) and his subsequent embrace of Buddhism.

 

• Chanakya (Option 4): Chandragupta's mentor and chief minister, not the ruler/founder of the empire himself.

question: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coulomb.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SI unit of electric charge is the Coulomb (C), named after the French physicist Charles-Augustin de Coulomb. (विद्युत आवेश की इकाई — कूलॉम)

 

• One coulomb is defined as the quantity of charge transferred by a steady current of one ampere flowing for one second (1 C = 1 A x 1 s).

 

• The charge on a single electron is approximately 1.6 x 10^-19 coulombs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coulomb's Law describes the electrostatic force between two point charges, which is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

 

NOTE

 

• Ampere (Option 1): The SI unit of electric current, one of the seven SI base units.

 

• Volt (Option 2): The SI unit of electric potential difference (voltage).

 

• Ohm (Option 4): The SI unit of electrical resistance.

question: Which international organisation publishes the 'World Economic Outlook' report?
option_4: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)
solution_text:
The correct answer is International Monetary Fund (IMF).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The World Economic Outlook (WEO) is a report published by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), typically twice a year (April and October, with interim updates in January and July), analysing global economic trends and providing growth forecasts. (विश्व आर्थिक दृष्टिकोण रिपोर्ट — IMF)

 

• The IMF was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference and is headquartered in Washington, D.C., USA.

 

• The IMF also publishes the Global Financial Stability Report and the Fiscal Monitor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The World Bank, also headquartered in Washington, D.C., publishes the Global Economic Prospects report.

 

• The IMF and World Bank are both often called the 'Bretton Woods Twins', having been created at the same 1944 conference.

 

NOTE

 

• World Bank (Option 1): Focuses on development financing; publishes Global Economic Prospects, not the WEO.

 

• WTO (Option 2): Deals with international trade rules and disputes, headquartered in Geneva.

 

• UNCTAD (Option 4): A UN body promoting trade and development; publishes the Trade and Development Report and World Investment Report.

question: In which of the following Vedas was Dasarajna war (the war of ten kings) mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rigveda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dasarajna (Battle of the Ten Kings) is described in the Rigveda, particularly in Mandala 7, attributed to the sage Vashistha. (दाशराज्ञ युद्ध — ऋग्वेद)

 

• The battle was fought on the banks of the river Parushni (modern Ravi) between the Bharata king Sudas and a confederacy of ten tribes (kings).

 

• Sudas, aided by the priest Vashistha, emerged victorious over the confederacy, which included tribes like the Purus, Yadus, Turvashas, Anus and Druhyus, among others.

 

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas, consisting of 1,028 hymns (suktas) organised into 10 Mandalas, composed in Vedic Sanskrit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rigveda is a key source for reconstructing the political and social history of the Early Vedic Period (c. 1500-1000 BCE).

 

• The rivalry between Vashistha and Vishwamitra, rival priest-sages, is also closely linked with the narrative of this battle.

 

NOTE

 

• Yajurveda (Option 1): Deals with the procedures and formulas for performing sacrificial rituals (yajnas).

 

• Samaveda (Option 2): Contains hymns meant to be sung/chanted, largely derived from the Rigveda, used in Soma sacrifices.

 

• Atharvaveda (Option 4): Contains hymns, spells, and charms related to everyday life, magic, and healing.

question: What is the percentage share of agricultural workers in India as per Census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 54.6%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, agricultural workers (cultivators plus agricultural labourers) constituted 54.6% of the total workforce of India. (कृषि श्रमिक — जनगणना 2011)

 

• Of the total workforce, cultivators formed about 24.6% and agricultural labourers about 30%, together making agriculture the dominant occupation category.

 

• This represented a decline from earlier censuses in the share of cultivators, alongside a rising share of agricultural labourers, reflecting increasing landlessness among the rural workforce.

 

• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census, conducted under the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Despite the high share of workforce in agriculture, the sector's contribution to India's GVA/GDP is much lower (around 15-18%), highlighting low agricultural productivity relative to employment share.

 

• Subsequent surveys (like the Periodic Labour Force Survey, PLFS) show the share of the workforce dependent on agriculture has continued to be significant, though the Census remains the definitive decadal source.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (64.6%, 44.6%, 55.6%) are incorrect and do not match the figure of 54.6% recorded in Census 2011.

question: Which state government launched 'Kaushalya Matritva Yojana' in March 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chhattisgarh government launched the 'Kaushalya Matritva Yojana' in March 2022 to promote institutional child birth and improve maternal and child health. (कौशल्या मातृत्व योजना — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• Under the scheme, pregnant women from the general category who deliver their second child as a girl child are given a cash incentive of ₹5,000, on the lines of an existing scheme for tribal women.

 

• The scheme aims to encourage families to welcome a girl child and to address the declining child sex ratio in the state.

 

• It was named after Kaushalya, the mother of Lord Rama, who according to legend belonged to the Chhattisgarh region (ancient Kosala).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhattisgarh has also run schemes like the 'Mukhyamantri Kaushalya Matritva Yojana' for tribal (Scheduled Tribe) women even before extending a similar benefit to general category women in 2022.

 

• Chhattisgarh is also known for schemes like 'Suposhan Abhiyan' and 'Narwa, Garwa, Ghurwa, Baadi' aimed at rural development and nutrition.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Runs its own maternal benefit programme, the Ladli Laxmi Yojana, but did not launch the Kaushalya Matritva Yojana.

 

• Haryana (Option 3): Runs its own girl-child schemes such as 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' initiatives; it did not launch this specific scheme.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Runs schemes like Kanya Sumangala Yojana, not the Kaushalya Matritva Yojana.

question: Who introduced the system of Dagh and Huliyah and cash payment to soldiers in the Delhi sultanate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alauddin Khalji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296-1316) introduced the system of Dagh (branding of horses) and Huliyah/Chehra (descriptive roll of soldiers) to prevent fraud in the army and paid soldiers directly in cash from the state treasury. (दाग और हुलिया प्रथा — अलाउद्दीन खिलजी)

 

• These reforms were part of his broader market control policies and military reforms aimed at maintaining a large, efficient standing army for his campaigns and to defend against Mongol invasions.

 

• Along with market regulation (price control on grain, cloth, horses, etc.), these army reforms allowed Alauddin Khalji to maintain a formidable army at controlled state expenditure.

 

• His administrative reforms are recorded by contemporary chroniclers such as Ziauddin Barani in the *Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alauddin Khalji also introduced the market control system (Bazar Niyantran Vyavastha) with officers like the Shahna-i-Mandi to regulate prices.

 

• He was the second ruler of the Khalji dynasty and successfully repelled multiple Mongol invasions during his reign.

 

NOTE

 

• Firuz Shah Tughluq (Option 2): Known for reintroducing the iqta system, digging canals, and founding cities like Firozabad; not associated with Dagh-Huliyah.

 

• Jalaluddin Khalji (Option 3): Founder of the Khalji dynasty, known for a lenient policy towards nobles and rebels, not for these army reforms.

 

• Ghiyasuddin Tughluq (Option 4): Founder of the Tughluq dynasty, known for administrative reorganisation but not specifically for the Dagh-Huliyah system.

question: Who found an empirical relationship between the half-life of alpha decay and the energy of the emitted alpha particles in 1911?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Geiger and Nuttall.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1911, Hans Geiger and John Mitchell Nuttall formulated the Geiger-Nuttall law, an empirical relationship between the half-life of an alpha-emitting radioactive isotope and the energy of the alpha particles it emits. (गीगर-नटल नियम — अल्फा क्षय)

 

• The law states that isotopes with higher decay energies have much shorter half-lives, and this relationship is roughly linear when plotted as the logarithm of the decay constant against the logarithm of the alpha particle range/energy.

 

• This empirical law was later theoretically explained by George Gamow (and independently by Condon and Gurney) in 1928 using quantum tunnelling, giving rise to the Geiger-Nuttall-Gamow theory of alpha decay.

 

• Hans Geiger is also well known for co-inventing the Geiger counter (with Walther Müller) for detecting ionising radiation, and for his role in the Geiger-Marsden (gold foil) experiment under Rutherford.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Geiger-Marsden experiment (1909), conducted by Geiger and Ernest Marsden under Ernest Rutherford's guidance, led to the discovery of the atomic nucleus.

 

• Alpha decay is a type of radioactive decay in which a nucleus emits an alpha particle (2 protons + 2 neutrons, i.e., a helium-4 nucleus).

 

NOTE

 

• Chadwick and Lawrence (Option 1): James Chadwick discovered the neutron (1932); Ernest Lawrence invented the cyclotron — neither is linked to this law.

 

• Fermi and Meitner (Option 2): Enrico Fermi worked on nuclear fission and beta decay theory; Lise Meitner co-explained nuclear fission — not this empirical law.

 

• Soddy and Aston (Option 4): Frederick Soddy proposed the concept of isotopes; Francis Aston developed the mass spectrograph — neither formulated the Geiger-Nuttall law.

question: Nati is a folk dance from which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nati is a popular folk dance of Himachal Pradesh, performed mainly during festivals, weddings, and harvest celebrations. (नाटी नृत्य — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• It is performed by both men and women in colourful traditional attire, in a large group, often set to the accompaniment of instruments like the dhol, nagara, karnal and shehnai.

 

• The Nati dance of Kullu (Himachal Pradesh) entered the Guinness Book of World Records in 2015 for the largest folk dance performance, with over 9,000 participants.

 

• Different regions of Himachal Pradesh have their own variants of Nati, such as Kullu Nati, Mahasu Nati, Sirmauri Nati and Kinnauri Nati.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Himachal Pradesh include Dangi, Chharhi, Thali and Jhoori.

 

• Himachal Pradesh's Kullu Dussehra is a major festival known for showcasing such folk performances, including Nati.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagaland (Option 1): Known for dances like the war dance of the Naga tribes, performed prominently at the Hornbill Festival.

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Known for dances/dance-dramas like Kathakali, Mohiniyattam and Theyyam.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Known for Kuchipudi (classical dance) and folk forms like Dappu and Lambadi.

question: Which of the following rivers is INCORRECTLY matched with its respective place of origin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sutlej - Dal Lake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sutlej river originates near Rakas Lake (Rakshastal), close to Lake Manasarovar, in Tibet, near Mount Kailash — NOT from Dal Lake, which is a lake in Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir unrelated to the Sutlej's source. (सतलुज नदी — राकस झील, तिब्बत)

 

• The Sutlej is one of the five rivers of Punjab and the longest of the tributaries of the Indus River; it enters India through Himachal Pradesh.

 

• The other three pairs given are correctly matched: the Mahanadi originates from the Sihawa/Amarkantak region (Dandakaranya highlands), Chhattisgarh; the Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier (Gaumukh) in Uttarakhand; and the Godavari originates near Trimbakeshwar, Nashik, Maharashtra.

 

• Since the question asks for the incorrectly matched pair, and Sutlej does NOT originate from Dal Lake, Option 2 is the correct choice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sutlej is also known as the Satadru, meaning "hundred channels", and its waters are harnessed by the Bhakra Nangal Dam.

 

• Dal Lake in Srinagar is fed by the Telbal Nallah, a stream originating in the Marsar Lake area, and has no connection to the Sutlej system.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahanadi - Sihawa Mountain (Option 1): This is a correctly matched pair; hence not the answer.

 

• Ganga - Gangotri glacier (Option 3): This is a correctly matched pair; hence not the answer.

 

• Godavari - Trimbakeshwar (Option 4): This is a correctly matched pair; hence not the answer.

question: Identify the animal that does NOT have bilateral symmetry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cnidarian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cnidarians (e.g., jellyfish, corals, sea anemones, Hydra) exhibit radial symmetry, where body parts are arranged around a central axis, NOT bilateral symmetry. (निडेरिया — अरीय सममिति)

 

• In radial symmetry, the body can be divided into similar halves by any plane passing through the central axis, which is suited to sessile or free-floating aquatic organisms that receive stimuli from all directions.

 

• Bilateral symmetry, by contrast, means the body can be divided into two mirror-image halves only along a single plane, and is a feature of more "advanced", actively moving animals with distinct head/tail and dorsal/ventral sides (cephalisation).

 

• Phyla like Annelida (segmented worms), Mollusca (snails, octopus, etc.) and Arthropoda (insects, crustaceans, etc.) are all bilaterally symmetrical.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Porifera (sponges) typically show asymmetry (no definite symmetry) or, in some cases, radial symmetry.

 

• Echinoderms (like starfish) show radial symmetry as adults but bilateral symmetry as larvae.

 

NOTE

 

• Annelida (Option 1): Segmented worms such as earthworms and leeches — bilaterally symmetrical.

 

• Molluscs (Option 2): Soft-bodied animals such as snails and octopuses — bilaterally symmetrical.

 

• Arthropoda (Option 3): The largest animal phylum, including insects, arachnids and crustaceans — bilaterally symmetrical.

question: The length of the pitch in cricket is________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 22 yards.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The length of a cricket pitch is 22 yards (20.12 metres), measured between the two sets of stumps (wickets) at either end. (क्रिकेट पिच — 22 गज)

 

• This measurement is also historically equal to one chain, an old English unit of length, and the pitch's width is 10 feet (3.05 metres).

 

• The rules governing the dimensions of the cricket pitch are laid down by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), the custodian of the Laws of Cricket.

 

• Each stump is 28 inches tall, and three stumps together with two bails form a wicket at each end of the pitch.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The distance from the bowling crease to the popping crease is 4 feet, and the popping crease extends 4 feet on either side of the return crease.

 

• Cricket is governed internationally by the International Cricket Council (ICC), headquartered in Dubai, UAE.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (20, 24 and 18 yards) do not correspond to the standard, official pitch length prescribed under the Laws of Cricket, which is fixed at 22 yards.

question: The________ National Voters' Day was celebrated across the country on 25th January 2023, with President of India Droupadi Murmu gracing the national level event held at New Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 13th National Voters' Day (NVD) was celebrated on 25 January 2023, with President Droupadi Murmu as the chief guest at the national event held in New Delhi. (राष्ट्रीय मतदाता दिवस — 13वां, 2023)

 

• National Voters' Day has been celebrated every year on 25 January since 2011, marking the foundation day of the Election Commission of India, which was established on 25 January 1950.

 

• The day aims to increase enrolment of voters, especially newly eligible young voters, and to promote awareness about informed electoral participation.

 

• The theme for the 2023 National Voters' Day was "Nothing Like Voting, I Vote for Sure".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Election Commission of India (ECI) is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution, responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India.

 

• The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) at the time of the 2023 National Voters' Day was Rajiv Kumar.

 

NOTE

 

• 12th, 10th and 11th (Options 2, 3 and 4): These would correspond to National Voters' Day celebrations in earlier years (2022, 2020 and 2021 respectively), not 25 January 2023.

question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acromegaly – Adrenaline.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acromegaly is caused by excess secretion of Growth Hormone (GH/Somatotropin) from the pituitary gland in adults, NOT by adrenaline; hence this pair is incorrectly matched. (एक्रोमेगाली — वृद्धि हार्मोन)

 

• It results in abnormal enlargement of the hands, feet, and facial bones (jaw, brow) due to excess GH acting on bones and soft tissues after the growth plates have fused.

 

• The other three pairs are correctly matched: Cushing's syndrome is linked to excess cortisol; Diabetes (mellitus) is linked to deficient/ineffective insulin; and Goitre (enlargement of the thyroid gland) is linked to abnormal thyroxine levels, typically due to iodine deficiency.

 

• Since the question asks for the pair that is incorrectly matched, Option 4 is the correct choice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Excess GH before puberty (before growth plate fusion) causes gigantism, whereas after fusion it causes acromegaly.

 

• Adrenaline (epinephrine), secreted by the adrenal medulla, is associated with the "fight-or-flight" response, not with acromegaly.

 

NOTE

 

• Cushing's syndrome – Cortisol (Option 1): Correctly matched; hence not the answer.

 

• Diabetes – Insulin (Option 2): Correctly matched; hence not the answer.

 

• Goitre – Thyroxin (Option 3): Correctly matched; hence not the answer.

question: Who was the Chairman of the Fifteenth Finance Commission of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NK Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• N.K. Singh was appointed as the Chairman of the Fifteenth Finance Commission, constituted in November 2017, with its recommendations covering the period 2021-26. (15वां वित्त आयोग — एन.के. सिंह)

 

• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body set up under Article 280 of the Constitution of India, tasked with recommending the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States.

 

• The 15th Finance Commission submitted its final report to the President in 2020, covering the five-year period from 2021-22 to 2025-26, and revised the states' share of the divisible pool.

 

• Each Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India every five years or earlier as deemed necessary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 under the chairmanship of K.C. Neogy.

 

• The 16th Finance Commission was constituted later, under the chairmanship of Arvind Panagariya, to cover the period from 2026-31.

 

NOTE

 

• Vijay Kelkar (Option 1): Chaired the 13th Finance Commission.

 

• YV Reddy (Option 3): Chaired the 14th Finance Commission; he was also a former RBI Governor.

 

• AK Chanda (Option 4): Chaired the Second Finance Commission (1956).

question: Noted dancer Birju Maharaj bagged the Filmfare award for best Choreographer for which film in 2016?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bajirao Mastani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj, the legendary Kathak exponent, won the Filmfare Award for Best Choreography (61st Filmfare Awards, 2016) for the song "Mohe Rang Do Laal" from the film Bajirao Mastani (2015), directed by Sanjay Leela Bhansali. (बिरजू महाराज — बाजीराव मस्तानी)

 

• Birju Maharaj was a foremost exponent of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak dance and received the Padma Vibhushan in 1986.

 

• Bajirao Mastani, starring Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone and Priyanka Chopra, was widely acclaimed for its grand choreography and won multiple technical awards that year.

 

• Birju Maharaj also choreographed dance sequences in other Bollywood films such as Devdas (2002) and Dedh Ishqiya (2014).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Birju Maharaj passed away in January 2022; he was also honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Kalidas Samman.

 

• The Filmfare Awards, instituted in 1954, are among the oldest and most prestigious film awards for Hindi cinema in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Befikre (Option 1): A 2016 Yash Raj Films romantic comedy directed by Aditya Chopra, unrelated to Birju Maharaj's choreography award.

 

• Dangal (Option 2): A 2016 sports drama starring Aamir Khan, unrelated to this choreography award.

 

• Mohenjo Daro (Option 3): A 2016 Ashutosh Gowariker film starring Hrithik Roshan, unrelated to this award.

question: The Sirpur National Dance and Music Festival is organised every year in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sirpur National Dance and Music Festival is organised annually by the Chhattisgarh government at the ancient archaeological site of Sirpur, located on the banks of the Mahanadi river in Mahasamund district. (सिरपुर राष्ट्रीय नृत्य महोत्सव — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• Sirpur was an important centre of Buddhist, Hindu and Jain heritage between the 5th and 10th centuries CE, and is known for structures like the Lakshmana Temple, Buddhist viharas, and monastic ruins.

 

• The festival showcases classical and folk dance and music performances by artists from across India against the backdrop of Sirpur's ancient monuments.

 

• Sirpur is being developed as an important archaeological and cultural tourism destination in Chhattisgarh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhattisgarh is also known for other cultural events such as the Bastar Dussehra and the Rajim Kumbh Mela.

 

• Sirpur was earlier known as Shripura and served as the capital of the Sharabhapuriya and Panduvamshi (Somavamshi) dynasties.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): Known for festivals like Sarhul and Karma, not the Sirpur festival.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Known for festivals like the Taj Mahotsav, not the Sirpur festival.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Known for the Khajuraho Dance Festival, not the Sirpur festival.

question: Which of the Five-Year Plans was prepared and launched by DP Dhar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fifth Five-Year Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79) was prepared and launched under D.P. Dhar, who served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission at the time. (डी.पी. धर — पांचवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• The main objectives of the Fifth Plan were "removal of poverty" (Garibi Hatao) and attainment of self-reliance, alongside promoting growth with social justice.

 

• The Plan was later terminated in 1978 (one year early) by the Janata Party government, which introduced a rolling plan instead of continuing it.

 

• The Fifth Plan also saw the launch of programmes like the Minimum Needs Programme (MNP) and Twenty Point Programme (20-Point Programme).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Planning Commission of India was set up in 1950 and was later replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

 

• The Rolling Plan concept, introduced by the Janata government (1978-83) after discontinuing the Fifth Plan, was proposed by economist Gunnar Myrdal.

 

NOTE

 

• Sixth Five-Year Plan (Option 1): Covered 1980-85, focused on removal of poverty and technological self-reliance; not associated with D.P. Dhar.

 

• Seventh Five-Year Plan (Option 2): Covered 1985-90, emphasised food, work and productivity; not associated with D.P. Dhar.

 

• Fourth Five-Year Plan (Option 3): Covered 1969-74, based on the Gadgil strategy of growth with stability; not prepared by D.P. Dhar.

question: In 2021, which State Government was in the news for planning to set up a Vedic Education and Sanskar Board to revive the knowledge of Sanskrit scriptures and Vedas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 2021, the Government of Rajasthan announced plans to set up a "Vedic Shiksha Board" (Vedic Education and Sanskar Board) to promote and revive knowledge of the Vedas and Sanskrit scriptures. (वैदिक शिक्षा एवं संस्कार बोर्ड — राजस्थान)

 

• The announcement was made by the state's Education Minister, aiming to formally recognise Vedic education imparted at gurukuls and Vedic pathshalas within the state.

 

• The board was intended to be set up within a few months and would work towards standardising curricula for Vedic and Sanskrit learning across recognised institutions in Rajasthan.

 

• The initiative reflects a broader push by several state and central bodies in India to institutionalise and mainstream traditional Vedic and Sanskrit education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• At the central level, the Maharshi Sandipani Rashtriya Ved Vidya Pratishthan under the Ministry of Education promotes Vedic studies across India.

 

• Rajasthan is also known for institutions like the Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University, Jaipur.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Not associated with this Vedic Education and Sanskar Board announcement.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 2): Not associated with this announcement.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Not associated with this announcement.

question: Which sector has the highest percentage share of goods exports in the annual GDP (at current prices) for the year 2020-21?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Engineering Goods.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among the major export categories, Engineering Goods held the highest percentage share of India's goods exports relative to the annual GDP (at current prices) for the year 2020-21. (इंजीनियरिंग वस्तुएं — सर्वाधिक निर्यात हिस्सा)

 

• Engineering goods — which include machinery, iron and steel products, auto components, and electrical equipment — have consistently been one of India's largest export categories in terms of value.

 

• The sector has benefited from schemes like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) and initiatives of the Engineering Export Promotion Council (EEPC) India.

 

• Other significant export categories for India during this period included petroleum products, gems and jewellery, and organic/inorganic chemicals, but Engineering Goods led in overall value/GDP share.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's overall exports of goods and services as a share of GDP stood at about 18.7% in 2020-21, rising to 21.4% in 2021-22.

 

• Major markets for India's engineering exports include the USA, UAE and European Union countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Electronic Goods (Option 1): A fast-growing export category, but did not have the highest share in 2020-21 compared to engineering goods.

 

• Drugs and Pharmaceuticals (Option 2): An important export sector (India is a major generic drug exporter), but its GDP share was lower than engineering goods.

 

• Organic and Inorganic Chemicals (Option 3): A significant export category, but again ranked below engineering goods in GDP share for that year.

question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
option_3: Article 19 – Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 19 – Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech and expression, along with rights to assemble peaceably, form associations, move freely, reside anywhere in India, and practise any profession, subject to reasonable restrictions. (अनुच्छेद 19 — वाक् स्वतंत्रता)

 

• Article 19 falls under Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution, specifically under the Right to Freedom.

 

• The other pairs listed are incorrectly matched: Article 15 actually deals with prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth; Article 17 deals with abolition of untouchability; and Article 14 deals with equality before law and equal protection of laws.

 

• Since Article 19 is correctly matched with freedom of speech-related rights, Option 3 is the correct answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 23 deals with the prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour, often referred to as the "right against exploitation".

 

• Article 18 deals with the abolition of titles, prohibiting the State from conferring titles other than military or academic distinctions.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 15 – Right against exploitation (Option 1): Incorrect; Article 15 actually deals with prohibition of discrimination, while right against exploitation is under Articles 23-24.

 

• Article 17 - Abolition of titles (Option 2): Incorrect; Article 17 deals with abolition of untouchability, while abolition of titles is under Article 18.

 

• Article 14 – Abolition of untouchability (Option 4): Incorrect; Article 14 deals with equality before law, while abolition of untouchability is under Article 17.

question: Where was the first All India Kisan Sabha formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lucknow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) was founded in Lucknow on 11 April 1936, during a session of the Indian National Congress. (अखिल भारतीय किसान सभा — लखनऊ, 1936)

 

• It was established to organise peasants against zamindari oppression and to voice demands for the reduction of rural exploitation and agrarian reforms.

 

• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was elected as the first President of the All India Kisan Sabha, and N.G. Ranga was its General Secretary.

 

• The Kisan Sabha adopted the Kisan Manifesto, which demanded, among other things, abolition of the zamindari system and reduction of agricultural rents and revenue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kisan Sabha movement was one of the earliest organised peasant movements in colonial India, and later influenced movements such as the Tebhaga movement in Bengal.

 

• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati is also known for founding the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929, a precursor to the All India body.

 

NOTE

 

• Lahore (Option 2): Associated with the Lahore Session of the Congress (1929), where the Purna Swaraj resolution was passed, not with the founding of the Kisan Sabha.

 

• Amritsar (Option 3): Associated with the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Amritsar Congress session (1919), not the Kisan Sabha's founding.

 

• Delhi (Option 4): Not the founding location of the All India Kisan Sabha.

question: U Srinivas is a famous player of which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mandolin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• U. Srinivas (Uppalapu Srinivas) was a renowned Indian musician famous for adapting the Western mandolin to play Carnatic classical music, earning him the title "Mandolin Srinivas". (यू श्रीनिवास — मैंडोलिन)

 

• He began performing publicly at a very young age and gained international recognition for pioneering the mandolin as a Carnatic concert instrument.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri (1998) and the Padma Bhushan (2010) by the Government of India for his contribution to Indian classical music.

 

• U. Srinivas collaborated with several international artists, including on projects associated with John McLaughlin's "Remember Shakti" ensemble, blending Carnatic and jazz/fusion music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• U. Srinivas passed away in 2014 at the young age of 45, but is remembered as one of India's most influential instrumentalists.

 

• Carnatic music, the classical music tradition of South India, traditionally uses instruments such as the veena, violin, mridangam and ghatam.

 

NOTE

 

• Violin (Option 2): Famous Carnatic violinists include Lalgudi Jayaraman and M.S. Gopalakrishnan, not U. Srinivas.

 

• Sitar (Option 3): Famous sitar players include Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Vilayat Khan.

 

• Guitar (Option 4): U. Srinivas is not known primarily as a guitarist; he is specifically renowned for the mandolin.

question: Who founded the independent State of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Murshid Quli Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Murshid Quli Khan is regarded as the founder of the independent/quasi-independent State of Bengal, having been appointed Diwan of Bengal by Aurangzeb and later becoming its Nazim (Governor/Subedar) in 1717. (मुर्शिद कुली खान — स्वतंत्र बंगाल)

 

• He shifted his capital from Dhaka to Murshidabad (named after him) and effectively made the province of Bengal function autonomously, paying only nominal allegiance to the weakening Mughal Empire at Delhi.

 

• He introduced significant reforms in revenue administration, notably the Jama Tumar system and the practice of advancing revenue-free loans (taqavi) to cultivators.

 

• He is considered the founder of the semi-independent Nawabi dynasty of Bengal, which continued through his successors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• After Murshid Quli Khan's death in 1727, he was succeeded by his son-in-law Shuja-ud-Din Muhammad Khan.

 

• The Bengal Nawabi line eventually ended with Siraj-ud-Daulah's defeat in the Battle of Plassey (1757) against the British East India Company.

 

NOTE

 

• Alivardi Khan (Option 1): Became Nawab of Bengal in 1740 after overthrowing Sarfaraz Khan; grandfather and predecessor of Siraj-ud-Daulah, not the founder of the state.

 

• Sarafraz Khan (Option 3): Son of Shuja-ud-Din, briefly Nawab (1739-40) before being defeated by Alivardi Khan.

 

• Shuja-ud-Din (Option 4): Son-in-law and successor of Murshid Quli Khan, not its founder.

question: Which of the following lines is NOT related to kabaddi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Attack line.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Attack line" is not an official line marked on a kabaddi court; the standard kabaddi court markings include the Baulk line, Bonus line, End line (and Mid line/Lobby), but not any "attack line". (कबड्डी — बॉक लाइन, बोनस लाइन)

 

• The Baulk line is drawn 3.75 m from the mid-line on each side and a raider must cross it while raiding for the raid to be considered valid.

 

• The Bonus line is drawn 1 m beyond the Baulk line; a raider who crosses it with at least one foot (in a valid raid) while remaining connected to their own half earns a bonus point.

 

• The End line marks the boundary at each end of the court, and the Mid line divides the court into two equal halves for the two competing teams.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A standard kabaddi court measures 13 m x 10 m for men (slightly smaller for women), divided into two equal halves by the mid-line.

 

• Kabaddi is governed internationally by the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF), and in India by the Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI).

 

NOTE

 

• Baulk line (Option 1): A genuine, officially marked line on the kabaddi court; hence not the answer.

 

• Bonus line (Option 3): A genuine, officially marked line on the kabaddi court; hence not the answer.

 

• End line (Option 4): A genuine, officially marked boundary line of the kabaddi court; hence not the answer.
